This process uses a biochemical conversion pathway that converts herbaceous biomass into ethanol via anaerobic fermentation and then upgrades the ethanol to HC fuels. The corn stover ethanol design uses dilute acid pretreatment followed by enzymatic hydrolysis and co-fermentation with recombinant Zymomonas mobilis. The corn stover is first treated with a dilute sulfuric acid catalyst at a high temperature (190°C) for a short time (2–10 minutes), liberating the hemicellulose sugars and other compounds. A purchased cellulase enzyme is added to the hydrolysate at an optimized temperature for enzyme activity. Several days (3–7 days) are required to convert most of the cellulose and xylose to ethanol. The “beer” liquor with approximately 4–8 wt % ethanol is then sent to recovery and purification, which uses standard adsorption technology. The solids after fermentation are separated and combusted in a fluidized bed combustor to produce high-pressure steam for electricity credits and process heat.
